- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon (especially first 5–10 days), then underestimates later — suggest adjusting for mean reversion toward historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), model tends to overshoot and overforecast for 1–3 days — apply dampening factor or lag correction for post-spike periods.
- Forecast tends to be too high in the first 10–15 days of the 30-day window — consider reducing initial forecast by 2–5% based on recent 7-day average.
- Model often fails to capture downward momentum in the last 5–7 days — add a downward bias adjustment if recent 5-day average is falling.
- Forecast shows persistent bias toward higher values — consider subtracting 1.5–3% of the 30-day average from final forecast if true outcome is consistently lower.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delay in model response to true price drops) — apply a 1–2 day lag correction for downward trends.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <80) — increase forecast by 1–2% for periods with low historical mean.
